# chainq: full reference

> Agent-first CLI for onchain and crypto market data. Public RPC endpoints with automatic fallback are built in; only `nft top` and long-tail NFT slugs need an API key. This file is the agent skill plus every per-domain reference in one page.

## Install

- One-liner: `curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sergio-prog/chainq/main/install.sh | sh`
- Homebrew: `brew install sergio-prog/tap/chainq`
- uv: `uv tool install chainq` / pipx: `pipx install chainq`
- Requires Python 3.12+ (the install script bootstraps uv). Update with `chainq update`.
- Teach an agent: `npx skills add Sergio-prog/chainq` installs the chainq skill.

## Output

- Default output is one plain line per result. Show it to the user as is.
- `--json` returns structured data to parse or compute over. `-f toon` is the same data in 2-3x fewer tokens; use it for long lists.
- `-q` prints the bare primary value. `-v` adds provenance: RPC endpoint, sources, explorer links.
- `-f table` aligns rows under headers for the user.
- Errors go to stderr with exit 1. With `--json`, the error is `{"error": "..."}` on stdout instead. Usage errors (bad flag or argument) exit 2.
- Partial failures are reported, not hidden. `portfolio` lists networks it could not reach in `unreachable` and failed price sources in `price_failures`. Rerun once before telling the user data is missing.
- A CoinGecko rate-limit error means wait a minute. It does not affect RPC commands.

## Finding the right command

`chainq schema` prints one usage line per command with every option. `chainq schema protocols hl --json` describes one subtree with types, defaults, and choices. Read the matching reference file below for usage notes before the first call in a domain.

| Question | Command | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Price, market cap, history, candles | `price`, `asset`, `candles`, `search`, `trending` | [market.md](#market-data) |
| Stablecoin supply and pegs | `stables` | [market.md](#market-data) |
| Token buybacks, ETF flows | `buybacks`, `etf` | [market.md](#market-data) |
| Wallet balance or net worth | `balance`, `portfolio` | [onchain.md](#onchain-evm-and-solana) |
| What an address is | `address` | [onchain.md](#onchain-evm-and-solana) |
| Gas, transactions, raw RPC, EVM utilities | `gas`, `tx`, `rpc`, `evm ...` | [onchain.md](#onchain-evm-and-solana) |
| Unknown token symbol | `tokens search` | [onchain.md](#onchain-evm-and-solana) |
| Where to earn yield on an asset | `yields --asset X` | [defi.md](#defi-yields-lending-dexs-protocol-metrics-nfts) |
| Lending markets, DEX pools, protocol TVL and fees | `protocols aave/morpho/kamino/pendle/uniswap/curve/aerodrome/llama` | [defi.md](#defi-yields-lending-dexs-protocol-metrics-nfts) |
| Staking and savings rates | `protocols lido/sky/ethena` | [defi.md](#defi-yields-lending-dexs-protocol-metrics-nfts) |
| NFT floors | `nft` | [defi.md](#defi-yields-lending-dexs-protocol-metrics-nfts) |
| Perps, funding, prediction markets | `protocols hl`, `protocols lighter` | [perps.md](#perps-and-prediction-markets) |

Networks: 27 EVM chains plus Solana. `-n` takes a key, alias, or chain id and defaults to ethereum; `chainq networks` lists them. Solana addresses, `.sol` names, and signatures route to Solana automatically.

Settings persist with `chainq config set <key> <value>` (API keys, `CHAINQ_RPC_<NETWORK>` overrides, timeouts); `config get`, `unset`, `list`, and `path` manage them. `chainq update` upgrades chainq, and `chainq version` prints the installed one.

## DeFi: yields, lending, DEXs, protocol metrics, NFTs

### Cross-protocol yields

```bash
chainq yields                           # sorted by TVL; minimum TVL defaults to $1M
chainq yields --asset usdc              # one asset across protocols and yield types
chainq yields --asset eth -n ethereum   # includes stETH staking
chainq yields --type lp -s apy          # sort: tvl | apy
chainq yields --min-tvl 0
```

Start "best yield on X" questions here. The `type` values (`lending`, `vault`, `staking`, `lp`, `fixed`) carry different risks: LP yields have impermanent loss and fixed yields expire. Say which type a rate is when comparing.

### Lending markets

```bash
chainq protocols aave markets -n ethereum        # reserves by size: supply/borrow APY, utilization
chainq protocols aave markets -c usdc -n base    # one asset, every Aave market on the chain
chainq protocols morpho markets -n base -c usdc  # supply/borrow APY, LLTV, utilization
chainq protocols morpho vaults -c usdc           # curated vaults: gross and net APY, TVL
chainq protocols kamino markets -c usdc          # Solana lending reserves; -c takes a symbol or mint
```

`-s` sorts by `supplied`, `supply-apy`, `borrow-apy`, or `utilization`. Aave data comes from Aave's official API and covers every market on the chain (Core, Prime, EtherFi on ethereum). Kamino covers lending reserves only, not wallet positions, strategies, or vaults.

### Fixed yield (Pendle)

```bash
chainq protocols pendle markets -n ethereum             # implied APY, LP APY, liquidity, expiry
chainq protocols pendle markets -c usde -s implied-apy  # sort: liquidity | implied-apy | expiry
```

Implied APY is the fixed rate you lock by buying PT. Compare `implied_apy_pct` from `--json`.

### Staking and savings rates

```bash
chainq protocols lido apr       # stETH APR (7d SMA), TVL, wstETH/stETH rate
chainq protocols sky rate       # Sky Savings Rate (sUSDS) and legacy DSR, read onchain
chainq protocols ethena yield   # sUSDe APY (current, 30d, 90d), USDe supply and peg
```

### DEX pools

```bash
chainq protocols uniswap pool weth usdc -n ethereum    # onchain state for v2, v3, and v4 fee tiers
chainq protocols uniswap pool eth usdc -V v4           # 'eth' is the native currency; -V v2|v3|v4|all
chainq protocols uniswap pool weth usdc --fee 500      # one tier: 100 | 500 | 3000 | 10000
chainq protocols uniswap pool 0xPoolAddress            # v2/v3 detected from the address
chainq protocols uniswap pools "weth usdc" -n ethereum # indexed discovery: 24h volume, liquidity
chainq protocols uniswap pools usdc -n base -s volume  # sort: liquidity | volume
chainq protocols uniswap stats                         # TVL and 24h/7d/30d volume
chainq protocols curve pools -n ethereum -l 10         # coins, 24h volume, base and CRV APY
chainq protocols curve pools -c usdc -s volume         # sort: tvl | volume | apy
chainq protocols curve stats                           # TVL, volume, fees, crvUSD TVL, CRV price
chainq protocols aerodrome pools -p cl --min-tvl 1000000  # Base; -p all | v1 (AMM) | cl (Slipstream)
chainq protocols aerodrome stats
```

- `uniswap pool` reads factory, pool, and StateView contracts, so its prices and reserves are authoritative. v4 reports price and in-range liquidity without reserves, and its deepest pools use native `eth`, not `weth`. Thin tiers can show stale prices; compare tiers before quoting one.
- `uniswap pools` ranks through DexScreener. Prefer addresses for long-tail tokens.
- Curve `apy_base_pct` is the swap-fee APY; `apy_crv_min_pct` and `apy_crv_max_pct` bound the CRV emissions (max is fully boosted). Curve covers 13 chains.
- Aerodrome `apy_base_pct` is swap fees and `apy_reward_pct` is AERO emissions.

### Any protocol or chain (DefiLlama)

```bash
chainq protocols llama protocol lido     # TVL, chains, fees, DEX volume
chainq protocols llama top -c Lending -l 10
chainq protocols llama chains
```

Use `llama protocol` for any protocol without a dedicated command; DefiLlama tracks thousands.

### NFTs (OpenSea)

```bash
chainq nft floor pudgypenguins azuki   # floor (native and USD), 24h volume, owners
chainq nft collection pudgypenguins    # floor, supply, volumes, contract, links
chainq nft top -s volume -l 10         # sort: volume | 7d-volume | market-cap | owners
```

Collections are OpenSea slugs, the last part of an opensea.io/collection/... URL. `floor` and `collection` work without a key for well-known collections. `nft top` and long-tail slugs need one: `chainq config set opensea-api-key <key>`.

## Market data

### Prices and assets (CoinGecko)

```bash
chainq price eth btc hype              # spot price, 24h change, mcap; symbols or CoinGecko ids
chainq price 0xTokenAddress -n base    # contract address; -n hints the network
chainq price <SPL mint>                # Solana mints work like contract addresses
chainq price btc eth --at 2025-03-01   # historical price on a date (last 365 days)
chainq asset ethena                    # profile: price, mcap/FDV, supply, ATH, links
chainq asset btc --links tradingview,binance,coingecko
chainq search "sky protocol"           # fuzzy name to CoinGecko id
chainq trending -l 10
chainq candles btc --days 30           # OHLC; granularity scales with --days (30d gives 4h candles)
chainq candles eth -d 7 -l 24 --json   # last 24 candles
```

- Use `price` for "how much is X" and `asset` for depth (supply, FDV, ATH).
- For an ambiguous or unknown symbol, run `search` first and pass the returned id.
- `price` and `asset` find contract addresses and mints through DexScreener, then pull CoinGecko data. A token CoinGecko does not list falls back to DexScreener pair data, marked `[dexscreener/<chain>]`, with price and mcap only.
- `--at` and `candles` need a CoinGecko-listed asset, and the public API covers only the last 365 days.
- `asset` prints a TradingView link by default. Set other defaults with `chainq config set asset-links binance,coingecko`.

### Stablecoins

```bash
chainq stables                          # ranked by mcap: peg price, 7d supply change, mechanism
chainq stables usde                     # one stablecoin, or a name filter
chainq stables -m crypto-backed         # fiat-backed | crypto-backed | algorithmic
chainq stables --min-mcap 1000000000
```

For depeg questions, read `price_usd` from `stables <symbol> --json` and compare it with 1.0. For "where to park stables", use `yields --asset <symbol>` ([defi.md](#defi-yields-lending-dexs-protocol-metrics-nfts)).

### Buybacks

```bash
chainq buybacks hype -d 30          # pick one or more programs; -d is the daily lookback (hype, sky, uni)
chainq buybacks hype sky uni        # several programs, each at its own cadence
chainq buybacks zro -f toon         # LayerZero, monthly rows
```

Programs are `hype`, `sky`, `uni`, `zro`, and `lit`. There is no default, so name the ones you need. Every row has `source`, `source_url`, `cadence`, and `provenance`; read `provenance` before quoting a number.

| Program | Data | Cadence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| hype | Hyperliquid Assistance Fund spot fills, live | daily |
| sky | Smart Burn Engine `Exec` events on Ethereum, live | about every 4h, bucketed per UTC day |
| uni | Firepit `Released` burn events on Ethereum, live | daily |
| zro | LayerZero tracker page, live, with a labeled snapshot if the page is down | monthly |
| lit | Returns a data limitation: Lighter treasury TWAP fills require auth | none |

The onchain programs (sky, uni) read Ethereum logs and take a few seconds.

### ETF flows

```bash
chainq etf btc -d 14       # daily US spot BTC ETF net flows, per issuer plus total
chainq etf eth --json
chainq etf btc -q          # latest day's net flow only
```

Rows carry `net_flow_usd` and one column per issuer. Data comes from The Block.

## Onchain (EVM and Solana)

Networks: ethereum, arbitrum, base, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, gnosis, unichain, linea, scroll, zksync, mantle, blast, sonic, berachain, worldchain, ink, soneium, celo, sei, hyperevm, monad, plasma, katana, robinhood, arc, and solana. `-n` also takes aliases (eth, arb, op, matic, bnb, avax, hype, rh, sol) and chain ids.

### Balances and portfolios

```bash
chainq balance vitalik.eth                         # native balance; ENS and .sol names resolve
chainq balance 0x... --coin usdt -n arbitrum       # token by symbol, or pass the contract address
chainq portfolio vitalik.eth                       # every network: native + every catalog token, USD total
chainq portfolio 0x... -n ethereum -n base --min-usd 10
chainq portfolio 0x... --all                       # include unpriced tokens and dust
chainq portfolio 0x... --defi                      # add Hyperliquid and Lighter equity and spot balances
chainq portfolio 0xA.. 0xB.. 0xC..                 # many wallets: wallet x network USD matrix
chainq portfolio -F wallets.txt --by total         # addresses from a file (one per line, commas ok; - is stdin)
chainq portfolio -F wallets.txt --by token --json  # one row per wallet and token
chainq portfolio --paste --by total                # addresses from the clipboard
```

- `portfolio` is the answer to "what's in this wallet" and "net worth". `total_usd` is in `--json`. Use `balance` for one token on one network.
- Multi-wallet views: `--by network` (default), `total`, or `token`. Order wallets with `-s balance|input|address`; `--short` abbreviates addresses.
- It sweeps the token catalog (thousands of tokens per network) with Multicall3, so holdings outside a curated list are found. Only catalog tokens are swept, which keeps airdrop spam out.
- Prices come from CoinGecko, then DefiLlama or Jupiter, then Pendle, then DexScreener with a $1k liquidity floor. Each asset carries `price_source` and `kind` (`token`, `atoken`, `stata`, `pt`, `yt`, `sy`, `lp`).
- Unpriced assets and assets below `--min-usd` (default $1) are hidden and counted in `hidden_assets`.
- Results are cached for 5 minutes per wallet and network; `--no-cache` rescans. A scan priced during a source outage is not cached.

### Token catalog

```bash
chainq tokens search cat -n base   # symbol or name; curated and exact matches come first
chainq tokens status               # catalog size, sources, cache age per network
chainq tokens refresh -n base      # re-download the lists (they refresh daily)
```

Symbols resolve against a curated registry first (so `usdc` is always the canonical USDC), then the catalog: CoinGecko per-network lists, Aave aTokens and stata tokens, Pendle PT/YT/SY/LP, and Jupiter-verified Solana mints. A symbol with several matches errors and lists the candidates; pass the address instead. Any ERC-20 or SPL mint works by address. If the lists cannot be downloaded, everything falls back to the curated registry.

### Address intelligence

```bash
chainq address 0xADDR -n base
chainq address 9WzDX...            # Solana: wallet vs program, owner program, token accounts
```

On EVM it reports EOA vs contract (with EIP-7702 delegation), proxy implementation (EIP-1967, EIP-1167, ZeppelinOS), the ERC-20 profile, tx count, native and catalog holdings with USD values (`holdings_hidden` counts unpriced ones), reverse ENS on ethereum, and an explorer link. Run it before interacting with an unknown address.

### Gas, transactions, RPC

```bash
chainq gas -n base                        # gas price, base fee, transfer cost in USD
chainq tx 0xHASH -n ethereum              # status, parties, value, fee, block, decoded ERC-20 transfers, called function
chainq tx 5UfDuX94A1Qfq...                # Solana signature: status, signer, fee, slot
chainq rpc eth_blockNumber -n optimism    # raw JSON-RPC; prints the JSON result
chainq rpc eth_getBlockByNumber latest false
chainq rpc getSlot -n solana
```

- For "is it a good time to transact", quote the transfer cost from `gas`.
- For "did my tx go through", check `status` and give the explorer link from `tx -v`.
- `rpc` parses params that are JSON literals and passes the rest as strings. Use it for anything chainq has no command for.

### EVM utilities

`chainq schema evm` prints the usage of each one:

- Chain state: `block-number`, `block`, `find-block`, `client`, `chain-id`, `nonce`, `code`, `storage`, `call`, `estimate`.
- Encoding and hashing: `abi-encode`, `abi-decode`, `sig`, `sig-event`, `keccak`, `hash-message`, `hash-zero`, `namehash`, `checksum`.
- Bytes and numbers: `to-hex`, `to-dec`, `to-wei`, `from-wei`, `shl`, `shr`, `to-bytes32`, `format-bytes32-string`, `parse-bytes32-string`, `parse-bytes32-address`, `from-utf8`, `to-utf8`, `max-int`, `min-int`, `max-uint`.

```bash
chainq evm sig 'transfer(address,uint256)'
chainq evm call 0xToken 'balanceOf(address)' '["0xHolder"]' --returns uint256 -n base
chainq evm abi-decode 'address,uint256' 0x...
```

## Perps and prediction markets

Both venues use public APIs; no key is needed. Funding is shown as an hourly rate and as APR. Negative funding means shorts pay longs.

### Hyperliquid

```bash
chainq protocols hl price BTC ETH                 # mark/oracle price, 24h change, volume, OI, funding
chainq protocols hl markets -l 10 -s oi           # sort: volume | oi | funding | change
chainq protocols hl funding                       # most extreme funding rates
chainq protocols hl funding BTC --history -D 30   # cumulative, mean, APR, and range over N days
chainq protocols hl positions 0xADDRESS           # account value, margin, positions with PnL and liquidation price
chainq protocols hl spot price HYPE PURR
chainq protocols hl spot markets -l 10
chainq protocols hl spot balances 0xADDRESS --min-usd 10
chainq protocols hl dexs                          # HIP-3 builder dexs (xyz, flx, vntl, ...)
chainq protocols hl markets --dex xyz             # builder dex markets: tokenized stocks, commodities
chainq protocols hl price TSLA --dex xyz          # names are dex:COIN; a bare COIN works with --dex
chainq protocols hl outcomes [QUERY]              # HIP-4 prediction markets; the Yes price is the implied probability
```

### Lighter

```bash
chainq protocols lighter markets -l 10 -s oi      # last price, 24h change, volume, OI, funding
chainq protocols lighter price BTC ETH
chainq protocols lighter funding
chainq protocols lighter positions 0xADDRESS      # account value, collateral, open positions
chainq protocols lighter spot markets
chainq protocols lighter spot price ETH LIT/USDC
chainq protocols lighter spot balances 0xADDRESS --min-usd 1
```

`spot balances` is the full view of what an address holds on Lighter. Each asset splits into `available`, `locked` (in open spot orders), and `margin` (perp collateral), priced at Lighter index prices. USDC `margin` is the same collateral `positions` reports, so do not add the two. The `positions` account value excludes spot holdings and non-USDC margin.

For a combined view, `chainq portfolio 0x... --defi` adds Hyperliquid and Lighter equity and spot balances to the onchain sweep.
